title: Those who loved found Him
hookLine: I tell the truth, listen all: those who loved found the Lord (Savaiye)

lines: I'M GOING TO TELL YOU THE TRUTH.
cards: A family dinner, a meeting, a wedding speech that's gone on a bit. People are half-listening, checking phones. Then someone stands and says: I'm going to tell you the truth now.
Everyone listen. The room goes quiet, because that's not a sentence you say lightly. It means everything up to now was warm-up.
One of the savaiye has exactly that sentence in it, after all the elephants and conquerors and cranes.

teach.h: I SPEAK THE TRUTH. LISTEN, ALL.
teach.b: Here it is, transliterated: saach kahoon sun leho sabhai, jin prem kio tin hee prabh paaio. Saach kahoon: I speak the truth. Sun leho sabhai: listen, all of you.
Jin prem kio: those who loved. Tin hee prabh paaio: they alone found the Lord. Two small details make this line.
First, hee, that little word. Not those who loved also found Him, among others. Only they.
After all the parades, the ascetics and the drums and the rituals, one road is left standing. Second, the tense. Found.
The verse doesn't speak like a theory about how someone might reach God.
It speaks like a witness reporting what has already happened. What kind of love? Sikhs hear it as prem, a whole-hearted longing for the One that changes how you live.
Guru Nanak has a saying in the Guru Granth Sahib that helps. In paraphrase: if you want to play this game of love, come to my lane with your head in your hand. So it isn't a soft feeling.
It costs. Sikh tradition remembers many who loved that way, all the way.

teach.h: LOVE THAT COSTS, AND STARTS SMALL.
teach.b: But the Gurus also show that love starts small: in seva, in langar, in how you treat the person in front of you.
You can't love God, Sikhs often say, and be careless with the people God made. It fits that the line closes the crane verse. You can fake stillness.
You can fake ritual. Love is the one thing that doesn't work as a performance.

how: Many Sikhs recite this savaiya each morning as part of the Tav Prasad Savaiye, and its closing line is widely quoted and sung in kirtan as a summary of the Sikh teaching on love.

o: whole-hearted love that changes how you live
a feeling of calm after long meditation
a vow of devotion made at initiation

games.q: those who loved — tap the pairs.

s: the line is in the future tense: those who love will find
it's past tense, a report: those who loved, found.
the small word hee means only, or they alone
after every parade, one road is left standing: love.
in Sikh teaching, this love is only a warm feeling
Guru Nanak's saying pictures coming with your head in your hand: love that costs.

games.q: after the elephants, the conquerors, the cranes and the rituals, the poet says, I speak the truth, listen, all of you. what comes next?
o: those who fasted longest found the Lord.
those who loved, they alone found the Lord.
no one has ever found the Lord.
games.why: jin prem kio tin hee prabh paaio: those who loved, they alone found the Lord. the line closes the crane savaiya and sums up all ten.

practice: Let a face come to mind, someone you love but haven't told lately: a parent, a sibling, a friend, a partner. Picture them clearly and find one specific thing you love about them.
If you pray, hold them in Waheguru; if not, simply hold them in your attention for a while.

wordCard.voice: Prem, whole-hearted love. Jin prem kio tin hee prabh paaio: those who loved, they alone found the Lord. The line the savaiye lean toward.

carryVoice: Your line: those who loved, found. Love that costs, and starts small. See you tomorrow, friend.
